Doesn't careful product thinking slow us down?

That's the worry Thesis is built around. The slow parts are writing tests, chasing evidence, and checking the work still matches the plan. Jev drafts the tests, they run in parallel instead of in a queue, your tools bring the evidence, and your agents keep it all current.
No. A doc is written to be approved. A thesis is a list of sentences you can test, and each one carries its own test and evidence.
Product managers, eng leads, and designers at remote teams of roughly 20 to 80 people, who already use tools like Linear, Notion, Dovetail, and Amplitude and have outgrown the PRD.
What does the AI do, and what doesn't it do?
Jev sorts each claim into desirability, usability, viability, or feasibility, and drafts the smallest test that could prove it wrong. It never marks an assumption validated. People log results.
Does a closed ticket prove an assumption?
No. Shipping something isn't evidence that it worked. Linear and Jira move a test's status. Only results, like a funnel, an experiment, or interview quotes, move the evidence score.
We're starting with Amplitude, PostHog, Dovetail, Linear, Slack, and Notion, one at a time with pilot teams. Tell us which one your team lives in when you request access.
Which agents can work in Thesis?

Anything that speaks MCP, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex, plus any agent that can make an HTTP request through the API. Each one uses a workspace token and shows up in activity under its own name. Agents can add and comment, but a person calls the result.
Export the thesis as an agent skill or a repo file so coding agents read the bets before they write code. Then Thesis checks each pull request and flags work that isn't tied to any bet.
We're running pilots with product teams of 20 to 80 people who want to move fast without guessing.
